LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 13.1.1 EXTENSIVE LISTENING: POEMS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.1: Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Extensive Listening: Poems
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Extensive Listening: Poems, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: what stands out in each group presentation. 1. How can you improve the presentation of a poem? 2. What messages are conveyed in poem?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify messages in poems,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Extensive Listening: Poems in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform poems using appropriate techniques,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Extensive Listening: Poems in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the role of poems in society. • Watch recordings or performances of poems on the need for consumer protection and patriotism for enjoyment, Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing • With peers, discuss the different messages in the poems, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views • Discuss in groups the performance techniques that make the presentations appealing, • Identify poems on the need for consumer protection and perform them while recording themselves, in groups, • Discuss, in pairs, what stands out in each group presentation. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Extensive Listening: Poems together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration is enhanced as the learner respects the opinion of others while discussing the different messages in the poems.

• Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner discusses what stands out in each group presentation thus enhancing performance.

Values:
Patriotism is fostered as the learner interacts with poems on consumer protection,

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Consumer literacy skills are enhanced as the learner interacts with poems on the need for consumer protection.
